title: Divisor-Lattice Fixed Fields of the Frobenius: fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ = 𝔽_{p^d} for d ∣ n
description: For a finite field K of characteristic p with prime subfield 𝔽_p = ZMod p and degree n = [K : 𝔽_p], this entry climbs the entire subfield lattice. For every divisor d ∣ n it identifies the fixed field of the cyclic subgroup ⟨frob^d⟩ generated by the d-fold Frobenius and counts its points: frob_pow_apply shows (frob^d) x = x^(p^d); mem_fixedField_zpowers_frob_pow_iff reduces 'fixed by ⟨frob^d⟩' to 'fixed by frob^d'; finrank_fixedField_frob_pow proves the degree drop [fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ : 𝔽_p] = d (Artin + tower law); card_fixedField_frob_pow / card_frob_pow_fixedPoints / card_pow_eq_self give the point count p^d in three guises; fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors shows distinct divisors give distinct subfields. Answers OQ-02-OQ-01-OQ-01, generalizing the parent's card_frob_fixedPoints from the single d = n case to every d ∣ n — the forward half of the bijection {subfields of 𝔽_{p^n}} ↔ {divisors of n}. 12 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.

originalContributions: frob_pow_apply: the d-fold Frobenius is the p^d-power map, (frob^d) x = x^(p^d), by induction on d (pow_succ + AlgEquiv.mul_apply + the exponent arithmetic p·p^d = p^(d+1)) — valid for every d with no divisibility hypothesis. This is what turns the abstract Galois power frob^d into the concrete map cutting out the solution set of x^(p^d) = x

mem_fixedField_zpowers_frob_pow_iff: being fixed by the whole cyclic subgroup ⟨frob^d⟩ equals being fixed by its single generator frob^d — the fixed-by-generator promotion (pow_fixed) specialised from frob to an arbitrary power frob^d, the step that makes Artin's finrank_fixedField_eq_card applicable to the concrete fixed-point set

orderOf_frob_pow: orderOf(frob^d) = n/d for d ∣ n, specialising orderOf_pow_of_dvd to the Frobenius via the parent's orderOf_frob = n — the order of the d-th power in the cyclic Galois group of order n

finrank_fixedField_frob_pow: THE DEGREE DROP [fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ : 𝔽_p] = d for d ∣ n. Artin's finrank_fixedField_eq_card gives [K : fixedField⟨frob^d⟩] = #⟨frob^d⟩ = n/d; the tower law n = [fixedField : 𝔽_p]·[K : fixedField] then cancels n/d (which is positive) to force [fixedField : 𝔽_p] = d. This is the heart of the divisor-lattice correspondence

card_fixedField_frob_pow / card_frob_pow_fixedPoints / card_pow_eq_self: the point count p^d in three equivalent guises (the intermediate field, the fixed-point subtype {x // frob^d x = x}, and the solution set {x // x^(p^d) = x}), via Module.card_eq_pow_finrank and the degree drop — generalizing the parent's card_frob_fixedPoints = p from d = n to all d ∣ n
fixedField_frob_pow_eq_pow_solutions: the fixed field of ⟨frob^d⟩ is, as a set, exactly {x | x^(p^d) = x} — the unique copy of 𝔽_{p^d} inside K, the elementary face of the Galois statement

fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors: the assignment d ↦ fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ is injective on the divisors of n — the forward (injective) half of the bijection {subfields of 𝔽_{p^n}} ↔ {divisors of n}, read off the point count p^d using that d ↦ p^d is injective for p ≥ 2

mathlibDependencies.description: Artin's theorem: for a finite-dimensional extension and a subgroup H of the automorphism group, finrank (fixedField H) E = Nat.card H. Gives [K : fixedField⟨frob^d⟩] = #⟨frob^d⟩, the input to the degree drop.
The tower law: finrank F K · finrank K A = finrank F A for a tower F ⊆ K ⊆ A. Applied to 𝔽_p ⊆ fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ ⊆ K to extract [fixedField : 𝔽_p] = d.
For d ∣ orderOf x with d ≠ 0, orderOf (x^d) = orderOf x / d. With the parent's orderOf_frob = n it yields orderOf(frob^d) = n/d.
For a finite-dimensional vector space over a finite field, Fintype.card V = Fintype.card K ^ finrank K V. With ZMod.card and the degree drop d it gives the point count p^d.
x ∈ fixedField H ↔ ∀ f ∈ H, f x = x. Reduces fixed-field membership to a universal statement over the subgroup, which mem_fixedField_zpowers_frob_pow_iff collapses to the generator.
For 2 ≤ a, the map a ^ · is injective on ℕ. With p ≥ 2 (p prime) it turns equal point counts p^a = p^b into a = b, giving injectivity over the divisors.

parentDependencies.description: frob x = x^p. The base case of the iterated-Frobenius identity frob^d = x↦x^(p^d).
orderOf(frob) = finrank (ZMod p) K = n. The input to orderOf_frob_pow = n/d.

overview.historicalContext: The Galois theory of finite fields culminates in a perfect bijection: the subfields of 𝔽_{p^n} correspond exactly to the divisors of n, with 𝔽_{p^d} ⊆ 𝔽_{p^n} iff d ∣ n. The parent entry pinned the two endpoints — the Frobenius generates the cyclic group Gal(𝔽_{p^n}/𝔽_p), and the field it fixes is the prime field 𝔽_p (the d = n rung). This entry fills in every rung between: for each divisor d, the power frob^d fixes the unique copy of 𝔽_{p^d} inside K, cut out by the equation x^(p^d) = x, with exactly p^d points. The whole picture is the fundamental theorem of Galois theory made concrete for the cleanest possible cyclic group.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (OQ-02-OQ-01-OQ-01, Frobenius endomorphism)**: Establish the full divisor-lattice correspondence — for every divisor d ∣ n = [K : 𝔽_p], identify the fixed field of ⟨frob^d⟩ as the degree-d subfield (the solution set of x^(p^d) = x) and count its p^d points, generalizing the parent's card_frob_fixedPoints from the single d = n case to all d ∣ n, and thereby exhibit the forward half of the bijection {subfields of 𝔽_{p^n}} ↔ {divisors of n}.

**Formalized**: frob_pow_apply ((frob^d) x = x^(p^d)); mem_fixedField_zpowers_frob_pow_iff and fixedField_frob_pow_eq_pow_solutions (the fixed field of ⟨frob^d⟩ is {x | x^(p^d) = x}); orderOf_frob_pow (orderOf(frob^d) = n/d); finrank_fixedField_frob_pow (the degree drop [fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ : 𝔽_p] = d); card_fixedField_frob_pow / card_frob_pow_fixedPoints / card_pow_eq_self (the count p^d); fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors (distinct divisors ↦ distinct subfields).
overview.text: A 219-line formalization climbing the entire subfield lattice of a finite field K with |K| = p^n. The mechanical heart is frob_pow_apply: the d-fold Frobenius is the p^d-power map (frob^d) x = x^(p^d), an induction on d. From it, mem_fixedField_zpowers_frob_pow_iff reduces being fixed by the whole cyclic subgroup ⟨frob^d⟩ to being fixed by its single generator frob^d (the fixed-by-generator promotion, now at an arbitrary power), so the abstract fixedField coincides with the concrete solution set of x^(p^d) = x (fixedField_frob_pow_eq_pow_solutions). The degree drop finrank_fixedField_frob_pow = d is then forced by two Mathlib pillars: Artin's finrank_fixedField_eq_card gives [K : fixedField⟨frob^d⟩] = #⟨frob^d⟩ = orderOf(frob^d) = n/d (orderOf_pow_of_dvd + the parent's orderOf_frob = n), and the tower law n = [fixedField : 𝔽_p]·(n/d) cancels the positive factor n/d to leave [fixedField : 𝔽_p] = d. Module.card_eq_pow_finrank converts the degree to the point count p^d, recorded in three equivalent guises (intermediate field, fixed-point subtype, solution set). Finally fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors reads off injectivity of d ↦ fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ from the distinct cardinalities p^d, exhibiting the forward half of the subfield ↔ divisor bijection. All 12 theorems verified with 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Iterated Frobenius**: frob_pow_apply proves (frob^d) x = x^(p^d) by induction on d generalizing x: the step rewrites frob^(d+1) = frob^d · frob, evaluates with AlgEquiv.mul_apply and the parent's frob_apply to (frob^d)(x^p), applies the inductive hypothesis at x^p, then closes the exponent arithmetic (x^p)^(p^d) = x^(p·p^d) = x^(p^(d+1)) with pow_mul and pow_succ'.

**Fixed field = single generator**: pow_fixed (generic fixed-by-generator promotion) plus mem_fixedField_iff and the parent's reduction of zpowers to nat-powers give mem_fixedField_zpowers_frob_pow_iff: x ∈ fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ ↔ (frob^d) x = x. Composed with frob_pow_apply this is fixedField_frob_pow_eq_pow_solutions.

**Degree drop**: orderOf_frob_pow rewrites orderOf_pow_of_dvd with the parent's orderOf_frob to get orderOf(frob^d) = n/d. finrank_fixedField_frob_pow then sets n = finrank (ZMod p) K, uses finrank_fixedField_eq_card and Nat.card_zpowers for [K : fixedField] = n/d, the tower law Module.finrank_mul_finrank for [fixedField : 𝔽_p]·(n/d) = n, and Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right (with n/d > 0 from Nat.div_pos and finrank_pos) to cancel against d·(n/d) = n (Nat.mul_div_cancel').

**Counting and injectivity**: card_fixedField_frob_pow combines Module.card_eq_pow_finrank, ZMod.card, and the degree drop; card_frob_pow_fixedPoints and card_pow_eq_self transport the count along Equiv.subtypeEquivRight. fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors deduces a = b from p^a = p^b (equal fixed fields ⟹ equal card) via Nat.pow_right_injective, using that divisors of the positive n are nonzero.
keyInsights: **The abstract power becomes a concrete map**: frob^d lives in the Galois group as an opaque group element, but frob_pow_apply identifies it as the honest map x ↦ x^(p^d). This is the bridge that lets the Galois-correspondence count of the fixed field be read as the elementary count of solutions of x^(p^d) = x.

**The degree drop is forced by two cardinalities, not constructed**: one never builds the subfield 𝔽_{p^d} by hand. Artin's theorem gives [K : fixedField⟨frob^d⟩] = #⟨frob^d⟩ = n/d, and the tower law turns that into [fixedField : 𝔽_p] = d by pure arithmetic cancellation. The subfield's size is a consequence of the subgroup's index.

**One inequality the lattice cannot see is built in**: the count p^d is correct precisely when d ∣ n; for a non-divisor the subgroup ⟨frob^d⟩ has order n/gcd(n,d) and fixes 𝔽_{p^gcd(n,d)} instead. Restricting to divisors d ∣ n is exactly what makes orderOf(frob^d) = n/d and the degree drop come out to d.

**Injectivity is a cardinality argument**: distinct divisors give distinct subfields not because the subgroups are visibly different, but because their fixed fields have different sizes p^d. The map d ↦ p^d being injective (p ≥ 2) is the whole proof of fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors — the cleanest possible witness of the subfield ↔ divisor bijection's injectivity.
prerequisites: The parent entry FrobeniusEndomorphismOQ02: the Frobenius frob ∈ Gal(K/𝔽_p), frob_apply (frob x = x^p), and orderOf_frob (orderOf frob = n = [K : 𝔽_p])
Galois theory of finite fields: the automatic IsGalois (ZMod p) K and FiniteDimensional instances, Artin's IntermediateField.finrank_fixedField_eq_card, and IntermediateField.mem_fixedField_iff
The dimension/tower formalism: Module.finrank_mul_finrank (tower law) and Module.card_eq_pow_finrank (card = base^finrank for finite vector spaces)
Finite cyclic groups: orderOf_pow_of_dvd (order of a power that divides the order) and Nat.card_zpowers (the cyclic subgroup ⟨a⟩ has order orderOf a)

sections.title: Overview and Setup
sections.summary: Module docstring framing the result as the full divisor-lattice correspondence, with the parent's d = 1 and d = n endpoints as the two extreme rungs. Imports Mathlib and the parent FrobeniusEndomorphismOQ02; fixes a finite field K of characteristic p over 𝔽_p = ZMod p of degree n.
sections.mathContext: $K$ a finite field, $|K| = p^n$, $\mathrm{frob}\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/\mathbb{F}_p)$ the prime Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$; the subgroups $\langle\mathrm{frob}^d\rangle$ run over divisors $d\mid n$.

sections.title: Part I: the d-fold Frobenius is the p^d-power map
sections.summary: frob_pow_apply: (frob^d) x = x^(p^d), induction on d (pow_succ + AlgEquiv.mul_apply + frob_apply, then exponent arithmetic p·p^d = p^(d+1)). frob_pow_fixed_iff: its fixed points are the solutions of x^(p^d) = x.
sections.mathContext: $(\mathrm{frob}^d)\,x = x^{p^d}$; fixed points are the roots of $x^{p^d} - x$.

sections.title: Part II: fixed by the cyclic subgroup ⟺ fixed by its generator
sections.summary: pow_fixed: fixed by a ⟹ fixed by every a^k (the generic promotion). mem_fixedField_zpowers_frob_pow_iff: x ∈ fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ ↔ (frob^d) x = x, via mem_fixedField_iff and the reduction of zpowers to nat-powers. fixedField_frob_pow_eq_pow_solutions: the fixed field of ⟨frob^d⟩ is, as a set, {x | x^(p^d) = x}.

sections.title: Part III: order, degree drop, and the point count p^d
sections.summary: finrank_pos (n > 0). orderOf_frob_pow: orderOf(frob^d) = n/d for d ∣ n. finrank_fixedField_frob_pow: THE DEGREE DROP [fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ : 𝔽_p] = d, via Artin's finrank_fixedField_eq_card ([K : fixedField] = n/d) and the tower law (cancel n/d). card_fixedField_frob_pow / card_frob_pow_fixedPoints / card_pow_eq_self: the count p^d in three guises, via Module.card_eq_pow_finrank.
sections.mathContext: $[\mathrm{fixedField}\langle\mathrm{frob}^d\rangle : \mathbb{F}_p] = d$ and $\#\{x : x^{p^d} = x\} = p^d$ for $d\mid n$.

sections.title: Part IV: injectivity over the divisor lattice
sections.summary: fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors: d ↦ fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ is injective on the divisors of n. Equal fixed fields force equal point counts p^a = p^b, and Nat.pow_right_injective (p ≥ 2) gives a = b — the forward half of the subfield ↔ divisor bijection.
sections.mathContext: $d\mapsto\mathrm{fixedField}\langle\mathrm{frob}^d\rangle$ is injective on $\{d : d\mid n\}$, since the counts $p^d$ are distinct.

crossReferences.description: The parent computes the fixed field of the single Frobenius (the d = n rung: fixedField⟨frob⟩ = 𝔽_p, card_frob_fixedPoints = p) and lists as its open questions exactly this generalization — fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ = 𝔽_{p^d} and #{x // x^(p^d) = x} = p^d for all d ∣ n. This entry answers both, with the degree drop, the three-guise count, and the divisor-injectivity capstone.

The grandparent proves frob generates the cyclic Gal(K/𝔽_p) and orderOf(frob) = n. This entry uses orderOf_frob = n together with orderOf_pow_of_dvd to get orderOf(frob^d) = n/d, the index that drives the degree drop.

The great-grandparent packages the Frobenius x ↦ x^p as a ring endomorphism with x^(p^n) = x. The iterated-Frobenius identity frob^d = x↦x^(p^d) here is the same iterate restricted to d ≤ n steps, now read as cutting out the subfield 𝔽_{p^d}.

mainTheorems.name: finrank_fixedField_frob_pow
mainTheorems.significance: The degree drop: the fixed field of ⟨frob^d⟩ has degree exactly d over the prime subfield — the heart of the divisor-lattice correspondence, forced by Artin's theorem and the tower law.

mainTheorems.name: card_pow_eq_self
mainTheorems.significance: The point count in its most elementary form: the equation x^(p^d) = x has exactly p^d solutions precisely when 𝔽_{p^d} ⊆ K, i.e. d ∣ n. Generalizes the parent's card_frob_fixedPoints = p (d = n) to all divisors.
mainTheorems.description: Exactly p^d solutions of x^(p^d) = x.

mainTheorems.name: frob_pow_apply
mainTheorems.significance: The d-fold Frobenius is the p^d-power map — the bridge identifying the abstract Galois power with the concrete map that cuts out the subfield 𝔽_{p^d}.
mainTheorems.description: Iterated Frobenius is the p^d-power map.

mainTheorems.name: fixedField_frob_pow_eq_pow_solutions
mainTheorems.significance: The fixed field of ⟨frob^d⟩ is, as a set, exactly the solution set of x^(p^d) = x — the elementary face of the Galois statement, the unique copy of 𝔽_{p^d} inside K.

mainTheorems.name: orderOf_frob_pow
mainTheorems.significance: The order of the d-th power of the Frobenius in the cyclic Galois group of order n — the index that, via Artin's theorem, becomes [K : fixedField⟨frob^d⟩].

mainTheorems.name: mem_fixedField_zpowers_frob_pow_iff
mainTheorems.significance: Reduces 'fixed by the whole cyclic subgroup ⟨frob^d⟩' to 'fixed by the single generator frob^d' — the step that makes the abstract fixed field coincide with the concrete fixed-point set.

mainTheorems.name: card_fixedField_frob_pow
mainTheorems.significance: The point count in intermediate-field form: the fixed field of ⟨frob^d⟩ is the copy of 𝔽_{p^d} with p^d elements, via Module.card_eq_pow_finrank and the degree drop.

mainTheorems.name: fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors
mainTheorems.significance: Distinct divisors give distinct subfields — the forward (injective) half of the bijection {subfields of 𝔽_{p^n}} ↔ {divisors of n}, read off the distinct point counts p^d.

references.text: Finite field — for each divisor d of n the subfield 𝔽_{p^d} ⊆ 𝔽_{p^n} is exactly the set of solutions of x^(p^d) = x, the fixed field of the d-th power of the Frobenius.
Galois group of a finite field — cyclic of order n, generated by Frobenius; the subfield lattice is the divisor lattice of n, with 𝔽_{p^d} ⊆ 𝔽_{p^n} iff d ∣ n.

conclusion.summary: Climbs the entire subfield lattice of a finite field K with |K| = p^n: for every divisor d ∣ n = [K : 𝔽_p], the d-fold Frobenius frob^d is the p^d-power map (frob_pow_apply), the fixed field of ⟨frob^d⟩ is the solution set of x^(p^d) = x (fixedField_frob_pow_eq_pow_solutions), it has degree exactly d over 𝔽_p (finrank_fixedField_frob_pow, via Artin + the tower law) and exactly p^d points (card_pow_eq_self and its two siblings), and distinct divisors give distinct subfields (fixedField_frob_pow_injOn_divisors). 12 theorems, 0 sorries and 0 axioms, no native_decide. Generalizes the parent's single d = n count to the whole divisor lattice.
conclusion.implications: This is the forward (injective) half of the fundamental bijection {subfields of 𝔽_{p^n}} ↔ {divisors of n}: each divisor d produces a distinct degree-d subfield 𝔽_{p^d}, cut out elementarily by x^(p^d) = x. Completing it to a full bijection requires the surjective half (every subfield of 𝔽_{p^n} is fixed by some power of the Frobenius), which follows from the fundamental theorem of Galois theory now that both the subgroups ⟨frob^d⟩ and their fixed fields are pinned. The same finite-field picture is the local model for Frobenius elements and decomposition groups in global Galois theory.
openQuestions: Prove the surjective half: every intermediate field 𝔽_p ⊆ L ⊆ K equals fixedField⟨frob^d⟩ for the divisor d = [L : 𝔽_p], upgrading the InjOn to a genuine bijection {subfields of 𝔽_{p^n}} ≃ {divisors of n} (the order-reversing lattice isomorphism)
Identify the subfield containment 𝔽_{p^d} ⊆ 𝔽_{p^e} ⇔ d ∣ e directly in terms of the Frobenius powers, as ⟨frob^e⟩ ≤ ⟨frob^d⟩ ⇔ d ∣ e, recovering the lattice (not just set) isomorphism
